messages:
maria: heads up — customer (acct: acme-inc) on Private deployment reporting debug bundle generation hangs. collector shows 'redacting' indefinitely, upload eventually fails with 403. request id: req_acme_01. can someone help collect repro steps and coord an upload?

alex: thanks — can you paste the exact collector command they ran and the minimal curl repro for the API call they said fails? also which upload mode are they using (s3/minio/sftp)?

maria: they used the packaged collector on their appliance. command they ran: `./redwood-collector --config /etc/redwood/collector.yml --collect debug --redact-rules /etc/redwood/redact.json`

maria: upload mode: s3 (minio behind LB). example failing upload error in logs: ```2026-07-06T14:02:11Z ERROR upload.s3: status=403 code=AccessDenied key=debug/acme/req_acme_01.tar.gz```

maria: curl repro for the API side they used to request a signed URL (their control plane is private -> internal url): ```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://internal-redwood.acme.local/v1/debug/presign -d '{"bundle_key": "debug/acme/req_acme_01.tar.gz"}'```

eng-collector: quick checklist: 1) collector binary should be run with `--log-level debug` and `--redact-dry-run` to validate rules, 2) capture `/var/log/redwood/collector.log` and `strace -f` if possible, 3) set `UPLOAD_DEBUG=1` to capture presign payloads.

ryan: +1 on checking presign payloads. also check that the presign role/account has kms:Encrypt/Decrypt for keys used by minio if they're using server-side encryption. i saw a similar 403 where the presign signed a different bucket name (LB rewrite). run `tcpdump -n host minio-host and port 9000 -w /tmp/minio.tcpdump` for a minute during upload if they can.

sam: also verify clock skew on the appliance — presigned URLs fail if system time is >5m off. `date -u` and `timedatectl status` quick checks.

maria: the customer ran `date -u` and it looks ok. attached a small collector log snippet: ```[2026-07-06T14:01:09Z] INFO redact: started rules=42
[2026-07-06T14:02:10Z] WARN redact: pattern missing for rule id=redact-pii-7
[2026-07-06T14:02:11Z] ERROR upload.s3: status=403 code=AccessDenied key=debug/acme/req_acme_01.tar.gz request_id=req_acme_01```

alex: that `pattern missing` is suspicious — if redaction errors out it can leave the file handle locked and the uploader retries then hits a presign mismatch. can you ask them to run collector with `--redact-dry-run` first and then `--collect debug --no-upload` to generate the tarball locally, confirm redaction succeeded, and then do a manual `curl` to upload to the presigned url. example manual upload: ```curl -X PUT "${PRESIGN_URL}" -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" --data-binary @debug_acme_req_acme_01.tar.gz -v```

maria: forwarded instructions. customer tried `--no-upload` and got a tar at `/tmp/redwood/debug_acme_req_acme_01.tar.gz`. manual upload to the presign still returns 403. they pasted the presign URL; it has `X-Amz-Credential=minio-user%2F20260706%2Fus-east-1%2Fs3%2Faws4_request` — looks like the presign credentials are for a different region/account.

eng-collector: if presign payload claims a different account, could be config on the private control plane pointing at an old minio endpoint. ask them to `cat /etc/redwood/control_plane.yml` and confirm `s3.endpoint` and `s3.bucket` match minio. also check `redwoodctl debug presign --bundle debug/acme/req_acme_01.tar.gz` locally on the control plane to see what we return.

ryan: I can take the tcpdump if they send it. if LB rewrites host header it may sign with the LB host vs backend minio host. check `x-amz-server-side-encryption` headers too.

maria: customer ran `redwoodctl debug presign ...` and it returned a URL with host `minio-backend.internal` but the LB terminates TLS and rewrites to `minio-proxy.acme.com`. they said they never rotated the signer credentials since the initial install last year.

sam: likely root cause: presign signer creds tied to backend host mismatch + stale signer keys. workaround: 1) temporary set collector `--no-redact` and `--no-upload` to get plaintext bundle and hand it to support via secure channel; 2) we can run a backend presign on their control plane if they can run `redwoodctl debug-presign --force` and paste output.

alex: for us to ingest the bundle safely we need a redacted copy. if they can't upload, ask them to scp the generated tar to our support sftp gateway (secured ticket). provide sftp target: `sftp-support.redwood.com:2222` (we'll open a temporary acct). sam, can you create temp sftp creds?

sam: created. creds sent to maria via secure DM. validity: 48h. :lock: :thumbsup:

maria: customer uploaded tar via sftp successfully. I pulled the bundle and ran `redwood-inspect --redaction-check /tmp/debug_acme_req_acme_01.tar.gz` — it shows 1 rule failed (redact-pii-7) because of a malformed regex in their custom redact.json. I fixed it locally and re-ran redaction with `--redact-rules /tmp/fixed_redact.json --no-upload` and the tar validated.

eng-collector: great — next steps: 1) recommend they rotate signer creds and ensure `s3.endpoint` and LB host align, 2) patch redact rule that referenced an invalid lookbehind, 3) we'll add a clearer collector exit code for 'redaction partial failure' in next patch to avoid ambiguous upload 403s.

support-bot: ticket TKT-8421 created for this escalation. link: https://redwood.support/tickets/TKT-8421 — assigned to alex, ryan. SLA: 24h.

alex: thanks team. marking this thread for postmortem and a short KB: "Private deploys: presign host mismatch + redaction partial failure". maria — can you paste final repro steps and logs into the ticket so we can compile KB?

maria: done — uploaded logs and the fixed redact.json to TKT-8421. customer happy with sftp fallback and will schedule a credential rotation. :white_check_mark:

ryan: leaving a note: when you have the control-plane config dump send it to eng-sre for a quick audit. I suspect we should add a presign host validation in the control plane.

maria: noted. closing thread here, will follow up in ticket if anything else pops up. :coffee:
